regime_classification.growth: {"dimension":"growth","metric_summary":"GDP 7.8% YoY; PMI 56.5","signal_text":"GDP at 7.8% YoY looks unambiguous until you notice the RBI's own full-year forecast sits at 7.1% YoY — a 70bps gap that implies the current quarter is borrowing from future quarters, not compounding them. PMI Composite at 56.5 is genuine, but core sector at 4.8% YoY (down from 5.0%) and IIP overall at 8.0% YoY suggest the goods economy is running below the services headline. The quality question: capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity is healthy but not yet at the 80%+ threshold that historically triggers private greenfield investment — so this expansion is real, but its durability depends on whether consumption sustains or credit tightening arrives first.","badge_label":"Expansion Mode","badge_type":"b-exp"}
regime_classification.inflation: {"dimension":"inflation","metric_summary":"CPI 6.09% YoY; Fuel 22.93% YoY","signal_text":"The headline CPI at 6.09% YoY — rising for three consecutive months from 3.21% — has now breached the RBI's 6% upper tolerance band, but the decomposition matters more than the number. Food inflation at 8.94% YoY is the primary driver; core CPI at 4.5% YoY is rising but still below the level that would force RBI's hand on its own. The trap: fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (95th percentile, three-year high) is feeding into WPI at 9.92% YoY with a lag — producer prices are already running hot, and the pass-through to core CPI in Q1 FY28 is not priced by the market. RBI's own inflation forecast of 5.1% YoY now looks optimistic by 100bps.","badge_label":"Inflation Overshoot","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.credit: {"dimension":"credit","metric_summary":"Credit 19.54% YoY; CD ratio 82%","signal_text":"Bank credit at 19.54% YoY against deposit growth of 16.86% YoY — a 268bps divergence widening for three consecutive months — has pushed the CD ratio to 82%, the 75th percentile of its 10-year range. The last time India sustained a CD ratio above 80% during a rate-cut cycle was FY14; within 12 months the taper tantrum forced 75bps of emergency hikes and NBFC funding costs spiked 150bps. Today's NBFC credit growth is already decelerating to 15.4% YoY from 15.8%, the first sign of funding stress. Corporate bond issuance at ₹1,34,000 cr / month confirms that large corporates are bypassing banks — the stress is being absorbed by the NBFC and mid-market banking segment, not the headline.","badge_label":"Deposit Gap Stress","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.policy: {"dimension":"policy","metric_summary":"Repo 5.25% p.a.","signal_text":"Repo at 5.25% p.a. with CPI at 6.09% YoY means the real policy rate is negative 84bps — the RBI is technically accommodative even as it describes its stance as 'data-dependent.' The inversion: a rate cut from here would widen the real-rate deficit further, accelerating deposit-to-equity migration and deepening the CD ratio problem. A rate hike to defend the 6% CPI ceiling would compress housing affordability (average home loan rate already at 7.35% p.a.) and risk stalling the capex cycle at exactly the moment capacity utilisation is approaching the private investment trigger. The RBI is not on pause by choice — it is pinned.","badge_label":"Rate Pause","badge_type":"b-neu"}
regime_classification.capex: {"dimension":"capex","metric_summary":"IIP CapG 16.9% YoY; CU 77.4% of capacity","signal_text":"IIP capital goods at 16.9% YoY (up from 16.1%) with capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity (up from 75.6%) is the most credible signal of a genuine investment upcycle — not budgeted capex, but actual machinery orders. Credit to industry at 19.5% YoY and credit to services at 28.3% YoY (83rd percentile, rising three consecutive months) confirm that banks are funding the expansion. The risk: core sector at 4.8% YoY — the infrastructure backbone of capex — is decelerating, not accelerating. If cement and steel dispatch don't follow IIP capital goods higher in the next two months, the investment signal is a leading indicator with no follow-through.","badge_label":"Capex Upcycle","badge_type":"b-exp"}
regime_classification.consumption: {"dimension":"consumption","metric_summary":"GST ₹231290 cr/mo; PV 32.1% YoY","signal_text":"GST at ₹2,31,290 cr / month (90th percentile) is the strongest collections print in the data set, but the composition requires scrutiny — a jump of this magnitude from ₹1,88,125 cr / month in one month typically reflects advance filings or year-end compliance, not a step-change in underlying demand. Passenger vehicle sales at 32.1% YoY and two-wheeler sales at 33.1% YoY are genuine demand signals, but both series show volatility (PV was at 7.9% YoY two months ago). The dual-economy read: vehicle sales strength is urban and semi-urban; the informal economy signal — two-wheeler registrations in Tier 3+ markets — needs to sustain for two more months before calling a broad consumption recovery.","badge_label":"Demand Surge","badge_type":"b-exp"}

signal_cards.1: {"signal_num":1,"signal_theme":"CREDIT CYCLE","status":"risk","title":"Deposit Gap Forces RBI's Hand","data_text":"Bank credit growth at 19.54% YoY (latest) vs deposit growth at 16.86% YoY — a 268 bps divergence widening for 3 consecutive months (13.8→17.1→19.4→19.54% credit; 10.8→17.8→16.86% deposits). CD ratio now 82% credit-to-deposits, up from 81% last month, at 75th percentile of 10-year range. NBFC credit growth decelerating to 15.4% YoY from 15.8%, signalling funding stress. Corporate bond issuance at ₹134,000 cr / month suggests corporates are bypassing banks.","implication":"Overweight private banks with CASA ratios > 45% — they'll poach deposits from weaker peers. Avoid NBFCs with wholesale funding > 30% of liabilities; they face margin compression and potential covenant breaches if deposit growth doesn't accelerate. RBI will likely ease liquidity via OMOs or CRR cuts within 2-3 months if this gap persists. Position for a 25-50 bps rate cut by Q3 FY27.","pct_10y":75,"pct_note":"CD ratio at 75th percentile historically preceded tighter liquidity and NBFC stress in 2018-19. Current divergence is the sharpest since post-COVID credit recovery.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.2: {"signal_num":2,"signal_theme":"CAPEX TRIGGER","status":"positive","title":"Capex Upcycle Broadens Across Sectors","data_text":"IIP capital goods at 16.9% YoY (latest), up from 16.1% YoY, with capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity (up from 75.6%), at 68th percentile of 10-year range. Credit to industry at 19.5% YoY (rising 2 of last 3 months: 19.2→20→18.2→19.5%), credit to services at 28.3% YoY (rising 3 in a row: 21.4→22.9→24.3→28.3%, at 83rd percentile), and credit to agriculture at 19.5% YoY (rising 3 in a row: 16.8→17→17.2→19.5%, at 82nd percentile). Core sector growth at 4.8% YoY, stable.","implication":"Overweight capital goods, cement, and steel stocks. Expect 12-18 month earnings upside in discretionary capex beneficiaries; lock in positions now before consensus catches up.","pct_10y":68,"pct_note":"Capacity utilisation at 77.4% is the highest in 3 years and historically signals 18-24 months of sustained capex. Last similar cycle (2014-15) delivered 40%+ returns to capex stocks before peaking.","is_surprise":false}

signal_cards.7: {"signal_num":7,"signal_theme":"UNDER THE RADAR","status":"surprise","title":"Office Absorption Collapse Signals GCC Shift, Not IT Weakness","data_text":"Office absorption at 4.02 mn sq ft / quarter (latest), down from 15.08 mn sq ft / quarter, at 0th percentile (signal: strong-negative, score: -100). However, Nifty IT index is flat (no significant decline), and office vacancy at 13.4% vacant (down from 14.5%, at 37th percentile, signal: neutral, score: 26). Rent in Bengaluru at ₹103.6 ₹/sqft/mo (61st percentile) and Mumbai at ₹156 ₹/sqft/mo (60th percentile) — both stable. Retail mall vacancy at 11.15% vacant (37th percentile, signal: neutral, score: 26). Contrast: airline passenger traffic at 8.64 mn / month (0th percentile, signal: strong-negative, score: -100) — a data anomaly suggesting measurement error, but e-commerce GMV growth at 25% YoY (43rd percentile, signal: neutral, score: -14).","implication":"Office absorption collapse is NOT an IT services crisis — it's a structural shift from traditional IT services to Global Capability Centers (GCCs) operated by multinational corporates. GCCs occupy smaller, more flexible spaces (co-working, flex offices) that don't show up in traditional office absorption metrics. This means: (1) Avoid betting on commercial real estate recovery via traditional office plays (Embassy, Mindspace, Brookfield REITs all down 12-35% YTD); (2) Overweight IT services companies with high GCC revenue (TCS, Infosys, HCL) — they're benefiting from GCC outsourcing without the capex burden; (3) Watch for a 'hidden' capex cycle in flex office operators and co-working platforms — they're the real beneficiaries. Falsifiable: if traditional office absorption rebounds to 10+ mn sq ft / quarter within 2 quarters, this thesis is wrong.","pct_10y":0,"pct_note":"Office absorption at 0th percentile is unprecedented in 10-year data, but paired with stable rents and falling vacancy, it signals a structural market shift rather than a demand collapse. This mirrors the 2020-21 flex office boom that preceded the 2022 correction.","is_surprise":true}

executive_summary.1:
{"para_num":1,"para_label":"India Macro Regime","para_html":"

GST Record Flatters — Services Credit Carries What Goods Cannot

The facts:

  • GST collections hit ₹2,31,290 cr / month (90th percentile), the largest single-month jump in the series, up from ₹1,88,125 cr / month.
  • PMI Composite at 56.5 and IIP capital goods at 16.9% YoY confirm expansion is broad — manufacturing and investment, not just services.
  • But core sector growth at 4.8% YoY (down from 5.0%) and CPI headline at 6.09% YoY — above RBI's 6% ceiling for the first time this cycle — introduce a policy constraint the growth data ignores.
  • Bank credit to services at 28.3% YoY (83rd percentile, rising three consecutive months) is doing disproportionate work; goods-economy credit to industry at 19.5% YoY is healthy but not accelerating.

The tension: GDP at 7.8% YoY and GST at a record look unambiguous; the RBI's own full-year forecast of 7.1% YoY and a CPI print that has now breached the tolerance band suggest the current quarter is front-loaded, not compounding.

Bottom line: Watch whether November GST sustains above ₹2,10,000 cr / month without advance-filing distortion — that is the test of whether demand is real or statistical.

"}
executive_summary.2:
{"para_num":2,"para_label":"Global Macro Regime","para_html":"

US Re-Accelerates, BOJ Tightens — EM Carry Trade Has a Clock

The facts:

  • US GDP SAAR accelerated to 3.4% SAAR (from 2.2%), US PMI Composite at 58.4 (80th percentile) — the US is not slowing.
  • But US CPI at 3.72% YoY (rising three consecutive months) and core PCE at 3.12% YoY mean the Fed at 3.88% p.a. is not done; the market pricing cuts is pricing the wrong Fed.
  • BOJ at 1.25% p.a. (100th percentile, rising two consecutive months) is the underappreciated tail: every 25bps from Tokyo unwinds yen carry positions that have funded EM equity inflows for 18 months.
  • Eurozone GDP at 0.4% YoY with ECB at 2.5% p.a. and CPI at 4.0% YoY — Europe is tightening into stagnation, removing a global demand buffer.

The tension: US re-acceleration keeps the Fed higher for longer; BOJ normalisation simultaneously drains the liquidity that funded the risk-on trade. Both forces point toward dollar strength and EM outflows — they are not offsetting.

Bottom line: BOJ's next meeting is the single most important global event for India FII flows; a third consecutive hike above 1.25% p.a. would be the trigger for EM de-risking.

"}
executive_summary.3:
{"para_num":3,"para_label":"Liquidity Conditions","para_html":"

SIP Autopilot Holds — But DII Absorption Has Halved

The facts:

  • SIP inflows at ₹32,160 cr / month (94th percentile) are stable over four months — retail systematic flows are not breaking.
  • But DII equity net flows collapsed to ₹6,222 cr / month from ₹51,829 cr / month two months ago — institutional domestic buying has largely stepped back.
  • FII equity net at -₹4,516 cr / month remains negative; the five-month sequence (-₹114 → -₹3,112 → +₹29,631 → -₹49,935 → -₹4,516 cr / month) shows no durable return of foreign conviction.
  • SIP YoY growth at 8.9% YoY (28th percentile, a 10-year low in growth rate) — the stock of SIP flows is high, but the incremental buyer is not arriving.

The tension: Headline SIP inflows look resilient; the growth rate of new SIP registrations at a 10-year low means the base is not expanding — the market is being held up by existing investors, not new entrants.

Bottom line: If DII net flows do not recover above ₹20,000 cr / month in December, the market loses its primary domestic shock-absorber against any FII selling episode.

"}
executive_summary.4:
{"para_num":4,"para_label":"Equity + Real Estate Implications","para_html":"

REITs Reprice Office Shock; Residential Splits by City and Ticket

The facts:

  • NRI buying is FALLING — NRI share of residential purchases at 18% (down 2pp), with NRI share within premium/luxury at 32%; remittances at $155.1 bn (14.5% YoY) provide macro support but deal flow is softening.
  • Premium ₹80 lakh–₹1.5 cr is the only ticket band where launch supply (31%) matches sales demand (31%); Hyderabad leads with sales +15% YoY and launches +120% YoY — a supply surge that will test absorption in 12 months.
  • Office absorption at 4.02 mn sq ft / quarter (0th percentile) is a statistical anomaly against city-level data showing Bengaluru at 5.2 mn sq ft / quarter (+11% YoY) and Hyderabad at 4.2 mn sq ft / quarter (+92% YoY); GCCs at 42% of occupier mix are replacing IT services at 22%.
  • Embassy REIT at ₹370/unit, Mindspace at ₹345/unit, Brookfield at ₹263/unit — all down 12–27% from prior prints — are pricing the aggregate absorption collapse, not the city-level GCC strength.

The tension: REIT unit prices are discounting an office market in distress; city-level leasing data shows Bengaluru and Hyderabad absorbing space at healthy rates. The market is pricing the wrong signal — aggregate vs. city-level divergence is the trade.

Bottom line: Bengaluru and Hyderabad office-exposed REITs are mispriced relative to their leasing data; watch Hyderabad vacancy (currently 11.8%) — if it crosses 15%, the GCC thesis breaks.

"}
executive_summary.5:
{"para_num":5,"para_label":"Key Risks to Monitor","para_html":"

Four Pressure Points — One Policy Trap

The facts:

  • CPI at 6.09% YoY has breached RBI's 6% ceiling with fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (95th percentile) still rising — the probability of a forced rate hike within two quarters is higher than the market prices.
  • CD ratio at 82% (75th percentile) with credit growing at 19.54% YoY vs deposits at 16.86% YoY — NBFC funding stress is the first transmission point; watch for RBI risk-weight circulars on unsecured lending.
  • BOJ at 1.25% p.a. (100th percentile) — a third consecutive hike unwinds yen carry trades and pressures INR at 92.59 ₹ (85th percentile) toward the 94–95 band, adding ₹12,000–15,000 cr / month to India's import bill.
  • Hyderabad residential launches at +120% YoY against sales of +15% YoY — unsold inventory at 28 months is the highest of any major city; a demand softening tips it into distress.

The tension: RBI is pinned between a CPI print above its ceiling (which argues for tightening) and a CD ratio that would amplify any rate hike into a credit crunch. The policy trap is not theoretical — it is the base case.

Bottom line: Watch December CPI: a print above 6.3% YoY forces RBI's hand and reprices the entire rate curve — that is the single most consequential data release of the week.

"}
